_comment: Out-of-scope questions for calibrating the groundedness check.
DRAFTED BY CLAUDE, REVIEWED BY MUZI LI.
These are questions the Canada Business Corporations Act cannot answer. A
correct system declines them. They are kept in a separate file from
eval_set.json because they measure a different thing: eval_set.json measures
whether the right provision is retrieved, and counting an unanswerable
question as a retrieval 'miss' would corrupt those numbers.
Difficulty matters more than quantity here. 'What is the capital of France?'
is trivial to decline -- nothing in a corporate statute is remotely close to
it. The cases that decide whether a threshold is any good are the
near-misses: questions about corporate law that this particular statute does
not govern. Those retrieve plausible-looking chunks with real similarity, and
a threshold tuned only on easy negatives will wave them through.

cases.question: how do I incorporate a company in Delaware?
cases.why: Corporate incorporation, but US state law. The CBCA governs federal Canadian incorporation and will retrieve its own incorporation provisions.

cases.question: what are the requirements to incorporate under the Ontario Business Corporations Act?
cases.why: Provincial statute. Nearly identical vocabulary to the CBCA, so retrieval will return confident-looking federal provisions.

cases.question: what do the CBCA regulations require of a distributing corporation?
cases.why: The Act defers this definition to the Regulations, which are a separate instrument and are not indexed. The Act itself only points at them.

cases.question: what are the continuous disclosure obligations under Canadian securities law?
cases.why: Securities regulation is provincial and separate from the CBCA, though the Act mentions distributing corporations and shareholder disclosure.

cases.question: what happens to shareholders when a corporation goes bankrupt?
cases.why: Governed by the Bankruptcy and Insolvency Act. The CBCA covers liquidation and dissolution, which is adjacent but different, and will retrieve those.

cases.question: can a corporation dismiss an employee without notice?
cases.why: Employment law. The Act is full of 'corporation' and mentions officers and employees, so retrieval will find surface matches.

cases.question: how are dividends taxed in the hands of a shareholder?
cases.why: Tax law. The CBCA governs whether a dividend may be declared, never its tax treatment.

cases.question: how do I file a patent application in Canada?
cases.why: Different area of law entirely, though still Canadian and statutory.

cases.question: should I incorporate my business or stay a sole proprietor?
cases.why: Asks for advice rather than the content of the law. A legal information tool should decline regardless of what it retrieves.

cases.question: what is the capital of France?
cases.why: Control case. If this is not declined, nothing is.

cases.question: who is the current Minister of Innovation, Science and Industry?
cases.why: The Act refers to the Minister throughout but never names one. Tests whether surface term overlap alone can trigger an answer.
